title: Design & Simulation of Engine Lifter Mechanism
description: Structural FEA, spatial optimization, and REBA ergonomic assessment of the valve lifter assembly for a Honda single-cylinder engine, completed during an internship at Atlas Honda.
objectives: Reduce peak von Mises stress in the lifter under cyclic valve-train loading
Optimize the spatial envelope of the mechanism within the existing cylinder head
Assess and improve operator ergonomics during assembly using REBA scoring
problemStatement: The existing lifter mechanism showed stress concentrations near the camshaft contact face and an assembly posture that scored poorly on ergonomic assessment, risking both part fatigue and operator strain on the line.
calculations: Static structural FEA with cam-profile-derived cyclic loading
Contact stress estimation at the cam-follower interface
REBA scoring across assembly posture stages
results: Lowered peak stress concentration at the critical contact face
Proposed envelope change compatible with existing tooling
REBA score improved from a high-risk to a low-risk posture band
lessons: Iterating between simulation output and shop-floor ergonomics constraints showed how structural optimization and human-factors design have to be solved together, not sequentially.

title: Combined Cycle Power Plant Design
description: Thermodynamic cycle design and performance analysis of a combined-cycle power plant, including Brayton-Rankine cycle coupling and heat-recovery steam generator sizing.
objectives: Model coupled Brayton and Rankine cycles for a target power output
Size the heat-recovery steam generator (HRSG) for the exhaust conditions
Evaluate overall plant efficiency against single-cycle baselines
problemStatement: Single-cycle gas turbine plants reject significant exhaust heat; the goal was to quantify the efficiency gain available from recovering that heat in a bottoming steam cycle.
calculations: First-law energy balances across turbine, compressor, and HRSG
Combined cycle efficiency vs. simple cycle comparison
results: Demonstrated efficiency gain over the single-cycle baseline
Defined HRSG pinch and approach temperatures for feasible sizing
lessons: Cycle-level thermodynamics rewards getting the pinch-point assumptions right before optimizing anything downstream.

objectives: Design a spaceframe chassis meeting FSUK Concept Class structural rules
Produce a compliant Design and Cost Bill of Materials (DBOM / CBOM)
Lead a student team through the technical submission cycle

FSUK cost multiplier application across a hierarchical part-numbering scheme
results: Completed spaceframe design meeting Concept Class rules

title: Two-Stage Helical Gearbox with Bearing Fault Detection And Diagnosis
description: Group project building a physically prototyped two-stage helical gearbox; led the machine learning side — vibration/sound feature extraction and a Random Forest classifier for autonomous bearing fault detection.
objectives: Extract time-domain features (RMS, kurtosis) from raw accelerometer and sound-sensor signals
Label and structure healthy vs. faulty bearing datasets across operating speeds for supervised learning
Train and validate a Random Forest classifier to autonomously distinguish healthy from faulty bearing states
Evaluate model performance via confusion matrix, feature importance, and learning-curve analysis
problemStatement: Continuous gearbox operation causes localized rolling-element bearing defects that must be caught before catastrophic failure. The challenge was to design and fabricate a working two-stage helical gearbox integrating gears, shafts, and bearings, then optimize it with a multi-sensor fault-diagnosis system rather than relying on manual inspection alone.
calculations: Transverse module derived from a 1.25 mm normal module at a 45° helix angle (mt = 1.7678 mm)
Stage 1: 13T/39T gear pair for a 3:1 ratio, pitch diameters of 22.98 mm and 68.94 mm, 45.96 mm center distance
Stage 2: 13T/52T gear pair for a 4:1 ratio, pitch diameters of 22.98 mm and 91.92 mm, 57.45 mm center distance
Combined system ratio of 12:1 across both stages
RMS and kurtosis feature extraction from accelerometer signals to quantify vibration energy and impulsive bearing-defect impacts
results: Built the FFT-based signal processing pipeline extracting RMS and kurtosis features from vibration/acoustic data
Trained a Random Forest classifier achieving ~97% bearing-fault classification accuracy
Confirmed via feature-importance analysis that z-axis vibration features carried the strongest fault signal
Validated the model generalized well despite background noise from the 3D-printed gear mesh and wooden housing damping
lessons: The biggest lesson was that model accuracy depended more on the mechanical setup than the algorithm choice — noise from the 3D-printed gears and housing resonance directly affected which vibration features were separable. Random Forest worked well here because it handled the non-linear, high-dimensional combined vibration/acoustic features without heavy tuning, but getting there meant close back-and-forth with the teammates handling the mechanical fabrication to understand what the sensor data actually represented.

title: Robotic Hand
description: A 3D-printed underactuated prosthetic hand prototype with tendon-driven fingers.
objectives: Design an underactuated finger mechanism driven by a single tendon per finger
Prototype a low-cost, 3D-printable prosthetic hand structure
problemStatement: Fully actuated prosthetic hands require a motor per joint, adding cost and weight; an underactuated tendon-driven approach can reduce both while still gripping a range of object shapes.
calculations: Tendon routing and finger linkage kinematics
Grip force estimation across finger joints
results: Working 3D-printed prototype capable of adaptive grip across varied object shapes
lessons: Underactuation trades precision for mechanical simplicity — tuning tendon tension turned out to matter more than the linkage geometry itself.
